_meta.purpose: Every formula your calculators need, with worked examples you can turn directly into unit tests.
_meta.note: These are mathematical identities, not tax law. They do not change year to year. The only judgement calls are rounding, compounding frequency and whether to show pre- or post-tax returns.
_meta.convention: All rates are annual nominal unless stated. n = number of periods. Round only at display time, never mid-calculation.

emi.name: Equated Monthly Instalment
emi.edge_case_zero_interest: If r = 0, EMI = P / n. Guard against division by zero.

amortisation_schedule.note: Float drift accumulates over 240-360 rows. Compute in integer paise, or force the final instalment to clear the residual balance exactly.

worked_example.note: Interest exceeds principal. Worth showing prominently - it is the single most useful thing an EMI calculator can tell a user.

prepayment_scenarios.reduce_tenure: Recompute n from the reduced balance holding EMI constant. n_new = -log(1 - (B*r)/EMI) / log(1+r)
prepayment_scenarios.reduce_emi: Recompute EMI from the reduced balance holding n constant.
prepayment_scenarios.guidance: Reducing tenure almost always saves more interest than reducing EMI. Show both, with the interest saved for each.

tax_interaction.self_occupied: Interest deductible up to Rs 2,00,000 under 24(b) - OLD REGIME ONLY. Principal within the Rs 1.5L 80C cap - OLD REGIME ONLY.
tax_interaction.let_out: Interest uncapped in both regimes, but in the new regime any resulting loss cannot be set off against salary or carried forward.
tax_interaction.app_idea: Show effective post-tax EMI cost by regime. This is a genuine differentiator over generic EMI calculators.

lumpsum_future_value.name: Mutual fund lumpsum appreciation
lumpsum_future_value.with_compounding_frequency: FV = P * (1 + r/m)^(n*m), where m = compounding periods per year
lumpsum_future_value.note: Mutual funds do not 'compound' at a stated frequency - NAV moves continuously. Annual compounding is the correct convention for projections.

sip_future_value.name: SIP future value (ordinary annuity, end of period)
sip_future_value.which_to_use: Most Indian SIP calculators use the ANNUITY-DUE form (multiply by (1+i)) because the instalment is debited at the START of the period. Pick one, state it in the UI, and be consistent. The difference on a 20-year SIP is material.

step_up_sip.name: Step-up / top-up SIP (annual increase)
step_up_sip.note: No clean closed form. Compute year by year and compound each year's accumulated balance forward.

worked_example.comparison: A flat Rs 10,000 SIP over the same period reaches about Rs 23.2 lakh. A 10% annual step-up reaches about Rs 33.5 lakh. This comparison is the most persuasive screen a SIP calculator can show.

swp.name: Systematic Withdrawal Plan
algorithm: if balance <= 0: corpus exhausted at this month
swp.sustainable_withdrawal: For a perpetual SWP, monthly withdrawal must be <= balance * i. Show the user the crossover point.
swp.tax_note: Each SWP withdrawal is a redemption and triggers capital gains on the units redeemed, computed FIFO. Equity: 12.5% LTCG above Rs 1,25,000/year, 20% STCG. Debt funds bought on or after 1 Apr 2023: slab rate regardless of holding period.

xirr.name: Extended Internal Rate of Return
xirr.why: The ONLY correct return measure for irregular cashflows - a real portfolio with SIPs, lumpsums, redemptions and switches. CAGR is wrong for anything other than a single in and a single out.
xirr.equation: 0 = sum over i of [ CF_i / (1 + rate)^((d_i - d_0) / 365) ]
xirr.method: Newton-Raphson, falling back to bisection when it fails to converge
implementation_notes: Seed the guess at 0.10. Newton-Raphson usually converges in under 20 iterations.
Bisection fallback over [-0.99, 10.0] is essential - portfolios with large early losses break Newton-Raphson.
Sign convention: investments negative, redemptions and current value positive.
The final row must be the CURRENT VALUE as a positive cashflow dated today.
xirr.xirr_vs_cagr: CAGR = (end/start)^(1/years) - 1 and is valid only for a single lumpsum. Never present CAGR on a SIP portfolio - it will be wrong and users who check elsewhere will lose trust in the whole app.

goal_planning.note: Do NOT approximate the real rate as nominal minus inflation. At 12% nominal and 6% inflation the approximation gives 6.00% but the correct figure is 5.66%. Over 25 years that error compounds into a materially wrong SIP target.

other_useful.rule_of_72: years_to_double = 72 / annual_rate_pct. Rough, good for intuition, never for a plan.
other_useful.effective_annual_rate: EAR = (1 + nominal/m)^m - 1, where m = compounding periods per year. Needed to compare a quarterly-compounded NSC against an annually-compounded PPF honestly.
other_useful.post_tax_return: post_tax = pre_tax * (1 - marginal_rate) for fully taxable interest (FD, NSC, SCSS, RBI bonds). Tax-free instruments (PPF, SSY) keep the full rate. Comparing an 8.2% SCSS against a 7.1% PPF without this adjustment is misleading for anyone in the 30% bracket.
other_useful.post_tax_worked_example: SCSS at 8.20% taxable at 30% plus 4% cess gives an effective 5.54%. PPF at 7.10% tax-free stays 7.10%. The apparently lower-yielding instrument wins comfortably for a high-bracket investor. This single comparison is worth building as a feature.

display_conventions.rounding: Round only at display. Currency to the nearest rupee; percentages to 2 decimals.
display_conventions.indian_numbering: Format as lakh and crore with Indian digit grouping (12,34,567), not Western (1,234,567). Users will not trust a rupee figure grouped the Western way.
display_conventions.disclaimers: Every projection screen needs: 'Returns are illustrative, not guaranteed. Mutual fund investments are subject to market risk.' Non-negotiable for a public-facing app.
